$comment: KNOWN-RED LEDGER (B266080). The e2e cases that are failing today and are NOT being fixed
in the run that recorded them. scripts/e2e-drift-gate.mjs compares each run against this
list and fails on EITHER side: a failure that is not listed is a NEW regression, and a
listed case that PASSES means the ledger is stale and must shrink.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The E2E workflow was red on 17 consecutive scheduled runs (every
weekday from 2026-07-22; last green 2026-07-21) and filed correctly every time — as 12
comments on one idempotently-reused issue (#762) that nobody answered for 17 days. The
alarm was not noisy, it was MUTE, and while every run was red a brand-new regression
would have changed nothing about the signal anyone saw. A list in the repo is reviewable;
a comment on a muted thread is not.
TWO LANES, because the two configurations do not see the same thing:
ci    — the scheduled workflow: SIGNED IN, against production planyr.io.
local — `npm run e2e` with no BASE_URL: LOGGED OUT, against a local build of the tree.
Measured head-to-head 2026-08-08 (ci run #41: 30 red · a full local sweep: 33 red):
25 red in BOTH  ·  5 red only in ci  ·  8 red only in local.
The 25 matter because they say these failures are NOT production or auth noise — they
reproduce on a plain local build with no account, so they are real and anyone can fix them.
The 13 that differ matter because neither lane substitutes for the other, so a case red in
one lane is no evidence at all about the other and the gate never lets one lane's entry
silence the other's failure. That gap is exactly how B1179's click-behavior and
inspector-close cases ended up with no watcher anywhere.
THE COUNT IS THE DEBT. It may fall freely; it grows only with --allow-grow --item B###.
The ci lane was seeded from run #41 (2026-08-07, 30 failed / 312 passed / 1 flaky).
module-keepalive's 'hidden headers ignore f' case was on this list at seeding and has been
REMOVED because it was fixed in the same change (B1179): the step that pressed Escape to
leave REAL browser fullscreen was written for the old chrome-hide `f` and headless Chromium
has no browser chrome to answer it. A fixed case never keeps its amnesty — that is the half
of the gate that stops this file becoming a permanent one.
THE LOCAL LANE was seeded from a full sweep run in the development sandbox on 2026-08-08, not
from a CI runner — the first honest measurement this configuration has ever had, since nothing
in the repo ran it before today. That sandbox blocks outbound GIS hosts, so a few of its 8
local-only rows may be artefacts of THIS environment rather than product breakage. They are
seeded anyway and deliberately: the gate's stale-entry half turns each artefact into a
one-line ledger shrink on the first real runner, which is cheaper and far more legible than
starting empty and reporting 32 'new regressions' that are nothing of the kind.
UPDATED FROM THE FIRST REAL RUN (#42, 2026-08-08) — this file is now measured, not seeded.
ci    29 → 30: five rows marked INTERMITTENT (see below, kept — they are still debt), and
one row ADDED — dim-callout-edit:90, which was already red in the local lane and is
now red in production too, so it is a genuine cross-lane failure the ci lane alone
could not have seen. The ci count went UP, and that is the gate working: a new
failure may only be recorded deliberately, with --allow-grow --item.
local 32 → 25: seven rows REMOVED because they genuinely pass on a real runner. They were
the sandbox's blocked-GIS artefacts, exactly as this file predicted when it was
seeded, and the gate's stale-entry half turned each into a one-line shrink.
INTERMITTENT rows carry evidence and are not an amnesty. Run #41 saw five cases fail after
two retries each; run #42 saw the same five pass. All reach an EXTERNAL GIS service, so they
flip with that service's availability rather than with the code. Their PASS is reported and
not fatal — otherwise this gate goes red on every wobble in somebody else's server, which is
the noise machine the whole item exists to dismantle. The marker requires two run numbers
that actually observed both outcomes; validateLedger() rejects it without them, so 'this one
is flaky' can never be asserted to silence something. The rows still count toward the debt.
SHRUNK 2026-08-08 BY B267536 — the pond-outlet / detention family, 20 rows out of EACH lane.
Every removed row is a case DRIVEN GREEN in a real browser before it was taken off this list;
none was removed on the strength of an argument. They were the whole pond/detention programme
(B900–B910) plus the yield panel: pond-outlet-render · -autosize · -clear · -compound,
pond-design-buttons, pond-detention-method, pond-inspector-layout, pond-land-earthwork and
yield-panel-layout.
WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG, because it matters that this was NOT an engineering defect. Every one
of the 20 failed in its SETUP — the step that opens the pond inspector and types a number into
it — and never reached the assertion it exists to make. The pond inspector was reorganised on
2026-07-21 (7ef3d3a5, B934, PR #744): the flat list of fields became collapsible groups that
start CLOSED, and 'Top-of-bank elev. (ft)' became the always-visible 'Rim' row. The workflow's
last green run was 2026-07-21 and it has been red every scheduled run since 2026-07-22 — the
next morning. Three later changes layered on: B969/B970 (2026-07-23) renamed one group,
B1188 (2026-07-30) made opening Properties a DOUBLE click, and B1414 (2026-08-04) renamed the
rail's 'Parcel ▾' button to 'Parcel tools ▾'.
Six specs each carried their own private copy of the same stale helper block, which is why one
UI change took out an entire family at once. Those copies are gone: the pond helpers live in
e2e/helpers.js now, so the next reorganisation is one edit rather than six.
NO ASSERTION WAS RELAXED TO GET HERE. The routed per-storm table, the Post ≤ Pre verdict, the
auto-size solve, the clear-and-reload persistence path and the honest overall FAIL all passed
on the first run that reached them — the engineering was never broken, it was unreachable.
The five copy assertions that HAD genuinely gone stale each name the commit that moved them,
in the spec, at the line that changed.
STILL RED, and named rather than left to be inferred: layer-point-hover-identify (4 ci · 2
local), canvas-gis-identify (1 ci, intermittent), contour-hover-elevation (1 ci · 1 local),
flood-district-scoping (1 ci · 1 local) and dim-callout-edit (1 ci · 1 local). The first two
families reach an EXTERNAL GIS service — the host this sandbox blocks outbound, and the same
service whose availability flipped five rows between runs #41 and #42 — so they are not
fixable here and are not evidence of a defect until a lane with egress says otherwise.
